speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hand-Foot-Mouth Disease (HFM) is unlikely given the age and duration; Erythema Multiforme (EM) or Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) are more probable triggers. Captopril is a known cause of SJS/TEN, but the location (forearm + mucosal) strongly suggests EM or SJS. Given the recent start of captopril and the specific symptoms, we must rule out SJS/TEN.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) secondary to captopril.

REQUEST TEST: CBC, CRP, ESR, Renal Function.
REQUEST IMAGES: Skin biopsy from forearm lesion.
